themes.label: Decrees
themes.rationale: The text mentions the ratification of a document and the order for it to be inscribed and displayed publicly in the agora, which is the standard procedure for a decree.
themes.quote: ἐὰν δ' ἐκεῖνος αὐτὸ κυρώσῃ καὶ στηλογραφηθῆναι αὐτ[ὸ] ἐπὶ τῆς ἀγορᾶς

themes.label: Edicts and Ordinances
themes.rationale: The inscription refers to a formal act of ratification by an authority and the establishment of a permanent record, typical of an edict.

themes.label: Laws and Regulations
themes.rationale: The text specifies that the document is to remain in place in perpetuity, suggesting a regulatory or legal nature intended for long-term enforcement.

themes.label: Stele
themes.rationale: The text explicitly mentions the act of inscribing the document on a stone stele.

themes.label: Fragmentary
themes.rationale: The presence of square brackets in the transcription indicates that parts of the text are missing and have been restored by editors.

themes.label: Worn / Weathered
themes.rationale: The inscription itself notes that older records had vanished or become illegible, which prompted this new inscription to preserve the text.
themes.quote: ἐπεὶ τινα τῶν παλαιῶν ἠφάνισται γραμάτων

persons.name: Ptolemy
persons.role: Individual mentioned in the document, likely a magistrate or official involved in the decree.

places.name: Agora
places.type: Public marketplace and location for the display of the stele.

rationale: This inscription from Battyna in Macedonia (dated to 193 AD) records the ratification of an official document and the command to have it inscribed on a stone stele for permanent display in the agora. The text explicitly justifies this action by noting that older records had disappeared or become illegible over time, emphasizing the need for a durable public record in perpetuity. The mention of Ptolemy likely refers to a local official or the proposer of the decree.
